Shapes.description: Stencils that render designs following shadcn/ui (Radix base, style nova, Inter, Lucide), with the style and theme chosen in the collection settings
Shapes.instructions: shadcn/ui Design. The style and theme in force are the collection settings (styleId, baseColor, accent, mode, radius, defaultFont); every default and every named style is evaluated against them when a shape is placed, and placed shapes never restyle afterwards. Every shadcn/ui variant and state (button variants and sizes, Focused / Invalid / Disabled, selected, checked, highlighted rows, text roles) is a named style of its base shape, listed in the shape's usage scenarios as @evolus.pencil.shadcn2026/<shortcut_id>. Put that name in the element's style field instead of writing colours. Set properties directly only for content (text, size, icons) or for a deliberately off-spec look. Every look is a plain property with Pencil's canonical names: fillColor, strokeColor and strokeStyle (the border or surface edge, written width|dash such as 1| for solid), textColor and textFont (the primary text), shadow (ShadowStyle dx|dy|blur|opacity|color) on floating surfaces, and named secondary slots such as focusRingColor or descriptionColor; no Enum ever selects a style. The corner radius is a Handle written r,0 (x is the radius in px). Changing a structural property (orientation, groupPosition, control, ...) or the disabled flag later does not recolour the shape, so apply the matching style again. The exceptions are `checked` on checkbox, radio, switch and choice_card and `active` on tab: those shapes hold separate unchecked and checked (inactive and active) colour sets, so set checked or active to true or false directly. Field content is also set directly: value and placeholder on input, textarea, select_trigger and input_group (the placeholder shows while the value is empty), the OTP value and activeSlot (1-based, 0 = no focused slot), and chips_input chips (one per line). A chips_input does not grow by itself: after writing chips, set box.h to max(minHeight, 2 × the strokeStyle width + 2 × paddingY + lines × chipHeight + (lines − 1) × gap), where lines is the number of wrapped chip rows (the chip input after the last chip needs inputMinWidth px on its row). Menus are stacks of atoms, not list properties: place a menu surface, then menu_label rows (24 high), menu_item rows (28) and the separator style menu_separator (9) on it, measured from the inner edge of its border (e, its strokeStyle width, 1 by default; the border is drawn inside the box): rows and labels e + 4 px inside its left and right edges, separators e px inside them (the full inner width), starting e + 4 px from its top; the menu height is 2e + 8 plus the atom heights. On menu_item set kind (action, checkbox, radio, submenu), checked, inset, label, shortcut and icon directly; checked only shows the check. Highlighted, destructive and command-selected rows and the menubar, combobox and command row geometries are named styles of menu_item; a select list row is menu_checkbox_item. command draws only its panel and search field: place command_heading (28), command_item (32) and separator (1 high, full inner width) atoms on it, rows e + 8 px inside its left and right edges, the first group heading at y = e + 44, where e is its strokeStyle width (0 for the inline command, 1 for command_dialog). Dialogs, menus and commands draw their edge inside the box, like inputs, so the box is the outer edge. A menubar holds menubar_trigger atoms 4 px inside it, 2 px apart; a navigation menu is a row of nav_menu_trigger atoms. Tabs are a tabs_list with tab atoms on it, 3 px inside: side by side with no gap (4 px apart on tabs_list_line, using the tab_line and tab_line_active styles), each as wide as its label plus 2 × (1 + paddingX) (Fit Width to Label) and 25 high in the 32 high list at the default 14 px font; on tabs_list_vertical the tabs are stacked, full inner width and 26 high (tab_vertical). Set active=true on the selected tab only; the tab panel is free content 8 px below the list. An accordion is a column of accordion_item atoms placed edge to edge, the last one in the accordion_item_last style (strokeStyle 0, no divider). An accordion_item does not grow by itself: after writing title, content or open, set box.h to 2 + 2 × paddingY + title lines × the textFont line height, plus, when open, content lines × the contentFont line height + contentPaddingBottom, plus the strokeStyle width (line height 20 and 43 for a closed one-line item at the default 14 px font). Pagination and breadcrumb have no shapes: build them from button (ghost page links, an outline one for the current page, previous and next with a chevron icon, 2 px apart) and from text and icon (muted links, a foreground current page and 14 px chevron-right icons, 6 px apart). Panels draw only their header: place body content and footer buttons as shapes on top. On dialog, the header starts e + 16 px inside and the tray footer (footerHeight) is drawn at the bottom; put its buttons 16 px inside the tray. On sheet, side is where it is docked (right, left, top, bottom) and its border is only on the opposite edge; content goes 16 px inside the border's inner edge, below the header (16 + title + headerGap + description + 16), and the footer buttons are full-width h-8 buttons stacked 8 px apart, 16 px above the bottom; drawer and drawer_right are its named styles, and a bottom drawer's header starts 20 px lower for the handle (showHandle). On popover, body content goes e + padding (10) inside, gap (10) below the header; hover_card has showHeader=false and holds free content e + 10 inside. tooltip does not size itself: side is where the tooltip sits relative to its trigger (top means above it), the box includes the arrow on the opposite edge (5 px at default size), and arrow is the arrow tip as a Handle written x,y on that edge (centred: w/2,h for top, w/2,0 for bottom, w,h/2 for left, 0,h/2 for right); after writing label or shortcut, set box.w to 12 + the label width + (shortcut ? 6 + the kbd chip width + 6 : 12), adding 5 for left or right, and re-centre arrow. toast is one sonner toast: title and description are single lines, icon is the type glyph (the named styles toast_success, toast_info, toast_warning, toast_error and toast_loading set it), actionLabel and cancelLabel show buttons at the right end when not empty; its height is 2 + 32 + max(19.5 for the title plus 20.2 with a description, 24 with a button), rounded. Cards, empty states, the sidebar, scroll areas, resizable panels and aspect ratios have no shapes of their own. card and card_sm are dialog styles: body content goes gap (16, or 12 on card_sm) below the description, footer buttons go padding px inside the tray, and footerHeight 0 removes the tray. empty is a dialog style with a centred header and no edge: place its buttons centred, gap (16) below the description; for the bordered look set strokeStyle 1|3,3. An item is a composition: an optional popover surface (showHeader false, shadow none, strokeStyle 0, radius 10,0; outline item: strokeColor of the border token and strokeStyle 1|; muted item: fillColor muted at 50 %; every variant keeps a 1 px border, transparent by default), content 13 px from its left and right and 11 px from its top (border plus px 12 and py 10), an optional 16 px icon 10 px before the text and 2 px lower when there is a description, a text title (weight 500, line height 1.375) with a description_text 4 px below it, and its buttons at the right end, 8 px apart. A sidebar is a sidebar_panel (256 wide) with a vertical_separator on its inner edge, or a sidebar_floating panel placed 7 px inside a 256 wide column (its rows are 16 px narrower, 224), or, for the inset variant, a sidebar_panel without the separator spanning the whole layout with a sidebar_inset main area on top of it, 256 px from its left and 8 px from its top, right and bottom. Groups sit 8 px inside the panel: a sidebar_group_label (32 high) followed by sidebar_menu_button rows (32, stacked with no gap), the current page in the sidebar_menu_button_active style. A menu badge is the row's shortcut text; kind submenu adds the trailing chevron; size sm is height 28 with a 12 px textFont, size lg is height 48. A menu or group action is a 16 px icon placed 6 px from the row's right end, with the row's label kept short of the icon. A sub-menu goes under its parent row: a vertical_separator 15 px from the row's left edge and sidebar_menu_sub_button rows (28 high, 4 px apart, starting 2 px below the parent row) 25 px from the row's left edge. a separator spans the panel 8 px inside it (panel width - 16); sidebar_input and sidebar_trigger go in the header, 8 px inside. Collapsed icon mode is a 48 wide sidebar_panel (a 52 wide sidebar_floating 7 px inside a 66 wide column) holding 32 x 32 sidebar_menu_button rows with an empty label and no badge, group labels, actions or sub-menus; a tooltip to the right shows a row's label. A scroll area is any content frame with a scrollbar_thumb (7 wide) 1 px inside its right edge, or along its bottom edge with width and height swapped, its length and offset showing the visible part. A resizable panel group is a frame with a vertical_separator (or a separator for stacked panels) between panels and, when it has a handle, a resize_grip centred on the line. aspect_ratio is a 16:9 muted area; for 1:1, 9:16 or 21:9 set box.h to the width divided by the ratio. A carousel is its slides (usually cards) with icon_button_sm buttons at radius 14,0 (chevron-left and chevron-right icons) centred vertically, 48 px outside its left and right edges. Badges, alerts, progress bars, skeletons, tables and calendars have no shapes of their own; avatar is the one data-display shape. badge, badge_secondary, badge_destructive, badge_outline, badge_ghost and badge_link are button styles (20 high, pill radius, 12 px text, a 12 px leadingIcon or trailingIcon); run Fit Width to Label after editing the label. alert and alert_destructive are dialog styles: mediaIcon is the leading icon (clear it for an alert without one), title and description are its two lines, and its height is 60 for one description line plus 20 per extra line. An alert action is a button_xs placed 9 px from the alert's top and right edges; keep the alert text short of it. progress is a slider style: drag valueHandle to the value (x = value percent of the width). skeleton (a 250 x 16 text line) and skeleton_circle (48) are popover styles; resize them to the content they stand for. A table is a stack of rows with a 1 px separator under every row except the last body row: the header row is 40 high with title_text cells centred vertically, body rows are 36 high with text cells 8 px from the row top (rows therefore start 37 px apart), and every cell's text starts 8 px inside its column (a checkbox cell has no right padding). A selected row puts a table_row_selected behind its cells; a hovered or expanded row and the footer row use table_row_tint, and the footer adds a separator above it and weight 500 text. The caption is a description_text 16 px below the table. Column widths follow the content. A calendar is 212 wide, on a popover or card surface or on its own: 8 px padding, a 28 high caption row with the month as a centred title_text and a calendar_nav_button at each end (chevron-right on the next button), 16 px below it a row of seven calendar_weekday labels (28 x 19, no gap), then the weeks: seven calendar_day cells (28 x 28, no gap), each week 8 px below the previous row. Six weeks give 212 x 295, five weeks 259. Days of the adjacent months use calendar_day_outside, today calendar_day_today, the selected day calendar_day_selected and unavailable days calendar_day_disabled. A range is a run of calendar_day_range_middle cells; its first and last days are calendar_day_selected placed over a calendar_day_range_middle strip 14 wide on the half facing the range. An avatar shows image when one is set, otherwise icon, otherwise the initials; avatar_sm (24) and avatar_lg (40) are its sizes (the Size: actions switch them), and showBadge adds a status dot in the bottom-right corner (badgeIcon check for a checked badge, hidden at sm). An avatar group is avatars with ringWidth 2 overlapping by 8 px, each placed after and over the previous one (24 px apart at the default size), ending with an avatar_group_count (initials +N, or icon plus). Chat family: a bubble is a textarea style (bubble, bubble_secondary, bubble_muted, bubble_tinted, bubble_outline, bubble_destructive) whose text is value. It does not grow with its text: set box w to the text width plus 2 x paddingX plus 2 (at most 80 percent of the message column) and box h to the line count times the textFont line height plus 2 x paddingY (41 for one line at 14 px); text beyond the box is drawn outside it. A ghost bubble is a plain text. Consecutive bubbles stack 8 px apart, and an end-aligned (user) bubble is right-aligned in its column. Reactions are a bubble_reactions (initials holds the emoji and the count) placed after the bubble, 12 px inside its right edge (or left edge), with three quarters of its height below the bubble's bottom edge. A message is a row: an avatar (32 at 14 px) at the bottom of the turn and, 8 px beside it, a column with 10 px gaps: an optional muted_header (name or time) starting 12 px in so it lines up with the bubble text, the bubbles or attachments, and an optional footer row of ghost_icon_button_xs (leadingIcon collection://vectors/copy.svg, thumbs-up.svg) also 12 px in; with a footer the avatar is raised by 32 so it lines up with the last bubble. An end-aligned message mirrors the row (avatar on the right, content right-aligned). Messages in a group are 8 px apart and groups 24 px apart. A message scroller is that transcript in a frame (for example 400 x 480, on a popover style or no surface) with a scrollbar_thumb at the right edge and, while not at the end, an icon_button_sm with leadingIcon collection://vectors/arrow-down.svg centred 16 px above the frame's bottom edge. An attachment is a dialog style: title is the file name, description the size or status, mediaIcon the file glyph (collection://vectors/file-text.svg) and the close button is the remove action, at the right and centred vertically; keep the title short of it. attachment_sm and attachment_xs are its sizes, attachment_idle (dashed), attachment_uploading and attachment_error its states. For an image attachment place an avatar over the media tile (box mediaSize x mediaSize, radius mediaRadius, strokeStyle 0|, image set). attachment_vertical is the card form (120 wide at 14 px, no close button): place a ghost_icon_button_xs 12 px inside its top and right edges, over the media, and for an image an avatar over the media tile. Attachments in a row are 12 px apart. A marker is a muted status line: an icon (16) and a description_text 8 px apart, vertically centred; marker_separator is the centred form between two lines (a date divider); the bordered form is that row with a separator 8 px below it. A questionnaire is a column with 16 px gaps: a muted_header progress line such as 1 of 3, a card_title question, a description_text, then the choices 8 px apart (questionnaire_choice, or questionnaire_choice_checkbox when several answers are allowed; set checked on chosen ones and strokeColor to the destructive colour on an invalid one; a questionnaire_shortcut key may sit 12 px inside the choice's right edge, 10 px from its top) or an input for a free answer, then an actions row: an outline_button Previous at the left, and an outline_button Skip and a button Next (or Submit) at the right, 8 px apart.
